narrative:
The model estimates a 78% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook were the availability of other job opportunities, your total years of experience across all roles, and the length of time you have spent in your current organization. Having received other job offers while employed here was the single biggest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving; it signals that you have attractive alternatives available. Your 6–10 years of overall experience also pulled the prediction in the same direction, as this mid-level tenure group is more mobile than both newer and much longer-serving employees. In contrast, your 6–10 years with this specific organization worked modestly in the opposite direction, slightly favoring staying, because many people who remain tend to have built similar or longer tenure here.

Taken together, these elements outweighed other considerations such as your satisfaction levels, training history, or work-life balance. The organization should review whether your current role can be made more compelling through clearer advancement paths or targeted retention discussions. You may wish to reflect on how those external opportunities align with your longer-term goals before making any decision. (218 words)
